title: Generation proves invertibility of the specified coefficient-action adjoint mate
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative ring and let $D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ be its ordinary unbounded derived module category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $C$ in degree zero. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be locally small triangulated categories with set-indexed coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $T_{\mathcal A}:D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})\times\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ and $T_{\mathcal B}:D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$ be bifunctors, exact in the first variable with specified coherent integer-shift comparisons, and with natural unit identifications $u^{\mathcal A}_K:T_{\mathcal A}(C,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and $u^{\mathcal B}_M:T_{\mathcal B}(C,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}M$.
Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be exact functors with a fixed adjunction $F\dashv G$ and counit $\epsilon:FG\to1$. Require their shift comparisons to be compatible with this adjunction, in particular
$$\epsilon_{M[n]}=\epsilon_M[n]\circ c_{F,n,GM}\circ F(c_{G,n,M}).$$
Suppose given a natural isomorphism
$$P_{V,K}:T_{\mathcal B}(V,FK)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(T_{\mathcal A}(V,K))$$
which commutes with the specified coefficient-variable shifts and satisfies
$$F(u^{\mathcal A}_K)\circ P_{C,K}=u^{\mathcal B}_{FK}.$$
For every $M$, assume that $A_M(V)=T_{\mathcal A}(V,GM)$ and $B_M(V)=G(T_{\mathcal B}(V,M))$ are exact functors preserving set-indexed coproducts, with their composite shift comparisons.

Define $\alpha_{V,M}:A_M(V)\to B_M(V)$ as the adjunction transpose of
$$F(T_{\mathcal A}(V,GM))\xrightarrow{P_{V,GM}^{-1}}T_{\mathcal B}(V,FGM)\xrightarrow{T_{\mathcal B}(1_V,\epsilon_M)}T_{\mathcal B}(V,M).$$
Then $\alpha$ is natural in $V,M$, satisfies $G(u^{\mathcal B}_M)\circ\alpha_{C,M}=u^{\mathcal A}_{GM}$, and commutes with all coefficient shifts:
$$c_{B_M,n,V}\circ\alpha_{V[n],M}=\alpha_{V,M}[n]\circ c_{A_M,n,V}.$$
For every $M$, the full subcategory $\mathcal L_M=\{V:\alpha_{V,M}\text{ is invertible}\}$ contains $C$ and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, distinguished cones, retracts and arbitrary set-indexed coproducts. One has $\mathcal L_M=D(C\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$, so every $\alpha_{V,M}$ is an isomorphism. This is an assertion about the specified transpose, with no claim that natural transformations are determined by their values on $C$. Here $c_{H,n,Z}:H(Z[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(Z)[n]$ denotes the specified shift comparison of a functor $H$.

proof.text: Write q_M = P.inv.app(GM) followed by TB.map(epsilon_M), a natural transformation TA.obj(GM) ⋙ F → TB.obj(M). Construct alpha_M as the composite of the right unitor inverse, the unit whiskered by TA.obj(GM), the associator inverse, and q_M whiskered by G. Its components equal the specified coefficientActionAdjointMate by Adjunction.homEquiv_unit. Naturality in V is now naturality of alpha_M. For naturality in M, apply Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_square: the inverse adjunct square follows from naturality of P.inv, functoriality of TB, and naturality of the counit.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation of the specified transpose from Zheng Construction 2.26.

proof.text: At $V=C$, projection normalization gives $P_{C,GM}^{-1}= (u^{\mathcal B}_{FGM})^{-1}F(u^{\mathcal A}_{GM})$. Naturality of $u^{\mathcal B}$ therefore gives $u^{\mathcal B}_M q_{C,M}=\epsilon_M F(u^{\mathcal A}_{GM})$. Transpose this equality: the left side corresponds to $G(u^{\mathcal B}_M)\alpha_{C,M}$ and the right side to $u^{\mathcal A}_{GM}$. Both unit identifications are isomorphisms, so $\alpha_{C,M}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; agent calculation of the specified transpose from Zheng Construction 2.26.

proof.text: For each K, hshift gives NatTrans.CommShift (P.hom.app K) ℤ componentwise. The inverse-isomorphism and composition instances, together with the assumed shift compatibility of TB.map(epsilon_M), give NatTrans.CommShift q_M ℤ. The unit of the adjunction commutes with shifts by adj.CommShift. The whiskering, associator and unitor compatibility instances therefore give NatTrans.CommShift alpha_M ℤ. NatTrans.shift_app_comm, rewritten using the component equality from step 1, is precisely the required shift equation for every integer n.

proof.text: Equip the enlarged module category with its Grothendieck abelian structure by transport across the ULift ring equivalence. Use [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] and the existing DerivedCategory.hasColimitsOfShape_discrete construction to supply source coproducts. For each M, apply [det-sf-determination-localizing] to the two exact coproduct-preserving coefficient functors and alpha_M, whose shift compatibility was proved in step 3. This gives its triangulated locus, closure under arbitrary coproduct cocones, and retract closure. Step 2 puts the degree-zero ring in the locus. Naturality under isomorphisms gives repleteness; equivalently, after step 5 every object lies in the locus, which proves each requested closure clause directly.

source.place: The full statement of det-sf-determination-localizing, applied in the coefficient variable.

proof.text: Every $C[n]$ belongs to $\mathcal L_M$ by steps 2 and 4. Apply [lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation] to the ring $C$. Its generating shifts and all three closure operations (set-indexed direct sums, third vertices of distinguished triangles, and retracts) lie in $\mathcal L_M$ by step 4. Thus every unbounded coefficient complex $V$ belongs to $\mathcal L_M$. This proves the conclusion for the specified transpose constructed in step 1; no uniqueness of natural transformations from their components on the generator has been used.
